title: Which conclusion the survey supports
subtitle: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments  · 1 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **1 of the official questions in Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments  are this one** — 1 Easy, 0 Medium, 0 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Easy tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- A random sample was drawn from a specifically defined group, and a strong result is reported, such as a large majority.
- The four choices are full-sentence conclusions: some describe the sampled group, some describe a broader or different group, and some reverse the condition that defined the group.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write down, in a few words, the defining condition of the group that was sampled.
- 2) Pick the conclusion about that same group, stated with a hedge such as 'most' rather than an exact figure.
- 3) Eliminate choices that widen the population or flip the defining condition.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a choice that extends the result to everyone in a broader category.
Or you pick one about the opposite group, reasoning that the opposite group would react the opposite way, which the data never tested.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
